effector: LexAop-TRPA1, 24-37 C heat ramp over 50 s
coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: off-target expression 10-20 neurons in abdominal neuromeres
quote: Activation of 1A interneurons via TRPA1 evoked forward locomotion. As the temperature ramped up, the decapitated flies started to walk
other_observation: Leg movements erratic, not in tripod gait, but with clear intersegmental coordination; locomotion occasionally interrupted by grooming bouts; rarely a fly would takeoff.
notes: d2-d4 unclear: walking implies leg movement but the source does not name which legs. d9 yes from 'interrupted by bouts of grooming'. d10 yes from 'Rarely, a fly would takeoff during the heat ramp.'

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1 lists this line under '2B' with off-target 'Expression in abdominal homologs of 2B neurons'; the Results text calls the hemilineage 2A
quote: they abruptly initiated high frequency flapping with the wings extended laterally in the flight position
other_observation: A few of the buzzing flies eventually went airborne; the authors state they do not know whether this was a jump via the T2 legs.
notes: d8 no: 'The decapitated flies typically stood in place'. d10 unclear: went airborne but source explicitly cannot say whether a jump occurred. d12 yes: wings held extended laterally in flight position during sustained buzzing. d9 yes: 'interrupted by a bout of wing grooming'.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: off-target ~10 weak neurons in thorax
quote: a subtle repositioning of the legs, with some repetitive, poorly coordinated leg movements and occasional grooming bouts
other_observation: Occasional wing flicking and wing scissoring movements.
notes: Text says the line is R23B05-GAL4; Supplementary file 1 gives R23B05-LexA, LexAop-TRPA1 for behaviour. d13 no: 'did not show high frequency wing buzzing'. Figure 9 gives 3B a large 'delta posture' bar, but the text calls it only 'a subtle repositioning of the legs' without saying flexion or extension, so d5/d6 unclear.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: 1-2 thoracic neurons/segment; ~30 abdominal neurons off-target
quote: the decapitated flies showed a progressive repositioning of their limbs so that they are closer to the ground by the end of the thermal ramp
other_observation: Spontaneous grooming appeared to be suppressed.
notes: 'their limbs' taken as all legs, so d2-d4 yes. d5 yes: body progressively lowered and held low (Figure 4R, 'splay out their legs' in the legend describes the same posture change). d8 and d11-d13 no: 'we observed no walking or wing associated behaviors'. d9 no: grooming suppressed.

preparation_detail: tethered intact flies gripping a Styrofoam ball
coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: 1-2 thoracic neurons/segment; ~30 abdominal neurons off-target
quote: Tethered intact flies that were gripping a Styrofoam ball responded to the temperature ramp by lowering their body position, thereby drawing the ball closer
notes: Separate experiment from the decapitated one: different preparation (tethered intact flies), so coded as its own record. d5 yes: body lowered and held (crouch, Figure 4 legend). Which legs moved is not stated, so d2-d4 unclear.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: ~5 weak cells/thoracic segment; ~30 abdominal neurons off-target
quote: poorly coordinated movements of the legs that often pitched the fly forward onto its anterior thorax
other_observation: Movements were not organized into any particular direction and became very erratic towards the end of the ramp; Figure 5D shows phasic repetitive movements of single limbs.
notes: d7 yes from Figure 5D legend 'phasic, repetitive movements of single limbs'. d12 no: wings 'usually only partially spread rather than in the extended flight position'. d8 no: movements not coordinated and not directed. Which legs is not specified, so d2-d4 unclear.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: weak expression in 1-2 neurons/thoracic segment off-target
quote: elicited a mixture of leg-related movements. Some showed a curving, forward movement while others pivoted in place
other_observation: Most flies did not move far enough (>one body length) to be classified as walking.
notes: d8 unclear: curving forward locomotion occurred but most flies fell below the source's walking criterion and the source does not call it coordinated walking. d11 no apart from grooming: 'There were no wing movements except for those associated with occasional grooming bouts' - grooming here is wing grooming, so d9 yes.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: <5 weak expressing neurons in abdomen, outside of 7B cluster in A1
quote: first the wings are raised, the mesothoracic legs then extend in a jump, and finally the wings depress and the fly begins to flap
other_observation: Flies continued spontaneous grooming with occasional wing flicking until they abruptly launched into the air; if they landed back on the hotplate they repeated the behavior.
notes: d3 yes: mesothoracic (middle) legs extend in the jump. d6 left not_assessed: the extension is part of a jump, not a held posture. d8 no: 'resulted in little walking behavior'. d12 yes: wing elevation/raising precedes the jump. d13 yes: flapping.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: ~2-4 neurons per abdominal neuromere off-target
quote: they also showed fidgety repositioning of their legs, but no walking or wing movements
other_observation: Activation 'had minimal effects on the behavior of the decapitated flies'; Figure 5M shows only minor positional changes through the period.
notes: d1 yes because fidgety leg repositioning and grooming are reported. d5/d6 unclear: Figure 9 gives 8A a 'delta posture' bar and Figure 5M reports minor positional changes, but neither says flexion or extension. d7 unclear: 'fidgety repositioning' is not explicitly called rhythmic or repeated. d11 no: 'no walking or wing movements'.

quote: a subtle change in posture in the decapitated flies as their legs became gradually more splayed out during the course of the heat ramp
other_observation: There was very little locomotion; occasional bouts of spontaneous grooming.
notes: 'their legs' taken as all legs, so d2-d4 yes. d6 yes: progressive splaying out of legs held for the ramp - Figure 9 classifies 9A as a pure 'delta posture' hemilineage. d5 no (legs splayed/extended rather than flexed). d7/d8 no: Figure 9 shows 9A with no uncoordinated leg movement or walking bar and the text reports very little locomotion.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: ~2-4 neurons per abdominal neuromere off-target
quote: dominated by leg movements. These movements were somewhat erratic, often causing the flies to make pivoting movements around a leg
other_observation: When there was net movement it was usually backwards; wings typically held back rather than in the flight position; rarely a fly would go airborne.
notes: d8 yes: the text refers to 'during walking' and the Discussion lists 10B among hemilineages evoking walking behavior (sustained walking). d7 yes: erratic, pivoting repeated leg movements. d12 no: wings held back, not in flight/extended position. d10 unclear: 'rarely a fly would go airborne' without a described jump.

penetrance: 100% takeoff (N = 13) for R26B05-GAL4 flies lacking tsh-GAL80
coverage_notes: Source: 'We were unable to construct lines to target hemilineages 11A and 11B independently, but R26B05-GAL4 targets the whole lineage'; the line occasionally showed expression in a bundle of descending interneurons; Supplementary file 1: 2-3 weak neurons/segment in thorax, small segmental sensory projections in abdomen
quote: the activation of the lineage 11 interneurons using R26B05-GAL4 evoked takeoff behavior
other_observation: Sequencing differed from normal takeoff: the decapitated flies commenced wing flapping prior to the jump.
notes: Covers both 11A and 11B because the line targets the whole lineage and the two could not be separated; record_type partial_or_mixed because of the descending-interneuron expression the source flags. A jump is reported but the source does not say which legs, so d2-d4 not_assessed.

penetrance: 9% of tsh-GAL80 flies (N = 22) took off, vs 100% (N = 13) without tsh-GAL80
coverage_notes: tsh-GAL80 suppresses the thoracic (lineage 11) expression while leaving expression in the descending interneurons (Figure 6-figure supplement 1B)
notes: Control variant of the lineage 11 experiment in which thoracic hemilineage expression is removed; takeoff largely abolished but still seen in 9% of flies, so d10 yes at low penetrance. Included as a separate line tested on this hemilineage, per protocol section 1 (one record per line tested).
quote: These decapitated flies showed a severe reduction in the number of takeoffs when subjected to the heat ramp

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: 1-2 neurons per abdominal neuromere off-target
locator: Results, 'Hemilineages 12A and 12B'; Figure 6J (27 C, 30 C, 35 C); Video 14
quote: started with walking behavior that was later joined by wing flicking and by the lateral extension and vibration of a single wing
other_observation: Resembled courtship singing of the male; eventually wing vibration frequency became extreme, wings usually not in flight position; flies would occasionally go careening into the air without an organized jump.
notes: One of the hemilineages marked (*) in Figure 9 as showing a progression of behaviors during the ramp. d12 yes: lateral extension of a wing held during vibration. d10 unclear: went airborne but 'there did not appear to be an organized jump'.

penetrance: 'little effect on some decapitated flies but evoked a tonic postural change in others'
locator: Results, 'Hemilineages 12A and 12B'; Figure 6M,N (dorsal and lateral views, 24 C vs 32 C); Video 15
quote: The T2 and T3 legs underwent an extreme extension and the legs froze in this position
other_observation: Flies either stayed rigidly upright or toppled over onto their side.
notes: d6 yes: sustained extension, legs frozen in position. d3/d4 yes (T2 and T3 legs); d2 unclear because 'The movements of the T1 legs were variable'. d5 no: extension rather than flexion.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: weak expression in about 10 neurons per thoracic neuromere off-target
locator: Results, 'Hemilineages 13A and 13B'; Figure 6S,T (24 C vs 37 C); Video 16
quote: they extended their legs progressively more to the side so that by the end of the heat ramp they were often resting on their coxae
other_observation: Described as a tonic postural change.
notes: 'their legs' taken as all legs, so d2-d4 yes. d6 yes: progressive, sustained lateral extension held to the end of the ramp; body also rests on coxae with tarsi elevated. d5 no.
